title: A full Kepler orbit gives less than 1.442 m/s of the early GJ 3341 residual if eccentricity is at most 0.4
abstract: We test whether higher harmonics of the known GJ 3341 planet can explain a previously selected 15.052-day residual in 61 early HARPS visits. A Fourier envelope bounds the full Kepler waveform for every orbital phase. For period 14.186 to 14.228 days, velocity semi-amplitude at most 5 m/s, and eccentricity at most 0.4, the contribution is below 1.442 m/s. The observed fitted amplitude is 2.262251 m/s. The bound includes the infinite harmonic tail and a margin between period grid points. It extends a prior bound that allowed only two harmonics. Direct Kepler trials and a separate Fourier identity check pass. These specified limits are not new confidence limits for the orbit. Noise, stellar activity and instrument errors can still explain the residual. No new planet or independent telescope confirmation is reported. Code, proof, aggregate results, figure, source hash and external data retrieval instructions are included. Source records remain outside the publication.

display.caption: Upper bound on the contribution from a full Kepler orbit to the previously selected extra wave. The bound covers all phases, K at most 5 m/s and period 14.186 to 14.228 days. The dashed line is the fitted observed amplitude. This is a deterministic model bound, not a signal significance test.
